title: Renting a home

items.title: The rent is stated clearly
items.look_for: A monthly rent figure, in digits and in words, and the date it is due
items.why_it_matters: A rent written two different ways is the most common source of disputes
items.question_to_ask: Can we write the rent in both digits and words, and say which date it is due?

items.title: The security deposit is stated
items.look_for: A deposit figure and what it covers
items.why_it_matters: The deposit is usually the largest sum you hand over
items.question_to_ask: How much is the deposit and what can it be used for?

items.title: There is a deadline for refunding the deposit
items.look_for: A number of days within which the deposit is returned after you move out
items.why_it_matters: Without a deadline you have no date to point to when asking for your money back
items.question_to_ask: Within how many days of handing back the keys will the deposit be refunded?

items.title: Deductions from the deposit are limited
items.look_for: What the owner may deduct, and whether normal wear and tear is excluded
items.why_it_matters: An open-ended right to deduct can consume the whole deposit
items.question_to_ask: What exactly can be deducted, and is ordinary wear and tear excluded?

items.title: The notice period is the same for both sides
items.look_for: How much notice each party must give to end the agreement
items.why_it_matters: A one-sided notice period leaves you exposed to a sudden move
items.question_to_ask: Can the notice period be the same for both of us?

items.title: Any lock-in period is clear and mutual
items.look_for: A minimum period before either side can leave, and what happens if you leave early
items.why_it_matters: A lock-in can cost you months of rent if your plans change
items.question_to_ask: Is there a lock-in, does it apply to both of us, and what does leaving early cost?

items.title: Any rent increase is capped and predictable
items.look_for: A percentage or figure by which rent rises, and how often
items.why_it_matters: An uncapped increase makes your future cost unknown
items.question_to_ask: By how much can the rent rise, and how often?

items.title: Who pays for maintenance and repairs is set out
items.look_for: Which repairs fall on the owner and which on the occupant
items.why_it_matters: Unassigned repairs become an argument at the worst moment
items.question_to_ask: Which repairs are yours and which are mine?

items.title: Electricity, water and society charges are assigned
items.look_for: Who pays each bill and how meters are read
items.why_it_matters: Society dues and electricity can add substantially to the monthly cost
items.question_to_ask: Which bills am I responsible for?

items.title: The owner must give notice before entering
items.look_for: A requirement to give notice before visiting the premises
items.why_it_matters: It protects your privacy and sets expectations on both sides
items.question_to_ask: How much notice will you give before visiting?

items.title: Registration and stamp duty are addressed
items.look_for: Who arranges registration and who pays the stamp duty
items.why_it_matters: An unregistered agreement is harder to rely on later
items.question_to_ask: Who will register the agreement and who pays the stamp duty?

items.title: The reasons either side can end it are listed
items.look_for: Events that allow early termination, and whether they apply both ways
items.why_it_matters: Broad termination rights on one side only leave you with little security
items.question_to_ask: On what grounds can each of us end this early?

items.title: Rules on guests and subletting are stated
items.look_for: Whether guests may stay and whether the premises may be shared
items.why_it_matters: A vague rule here can be used as grounds to end the agreement
items.question_to_ask: Can family or friends stay with me, and for how long?

items.title: How disputes are handled is stated
items.look_for: A named city, court or arbitration process
items.why_it_matters: A far-away forum makes a small dispute expensive to pursue
items.question_to_ask: Where would a dispute be heard?

suggested_questions: How much is the security deposit and when do I get it back?
What notice do I have to give before leaving?
Can the rent be increased during the agreement?
What happens if I need to leave during the lock-in period?

scenarios.title: I want to leave before the lock-in ends
I pay the rent a few days late
The deposit is not returned after I move out
The owner sells the flat during my stay

facts_to_have_ready: The date you moved in and the date you plan to move out
How much deposit you paid and how you paid it
Rent receipts or bank transfer records
Photographs of the condition of the premises
Any messages about repairs or the deposit
documents_to_bring: The signed agreement and any registration receipt
Electricity and society bills in your name
Any written notice you sent or received
